title: Apple: a publicly disclosed assembly dependency
caseType: Historical public case study — not a current alert

source.reliability: Original company statement about its operations
source.credibility: Attributable company report; not independent capacity measurement

dependency.facility: Primary assembly facility in Zhengzhou, China
dependency.basis: Apple explicitly identified this facility and these products in the dated statement.

observation: Apple reported temporary COVID-19 restrictions and significantly reduced capacity at the facility.
implication: Apple expected lower shipments than previously anticipated and longer customer wait times. This was a company forward-looking statement, not a verified eventual outcome.
classification: Confirmed observation of an attributable company statement; operational claim company-reported

options.label: Review delivery commitments
options.consideration: Compare customer commitments with written supplier delivery updates before promising dates.
options.tradeoff: Changing promises may affect customers; no cost or benefit quantified.

options.label: Review inventory exposure
options.consideration: Check available stock and substitute-product suitability against actual customer requirements.
options.tradeoff: Holding or sourcing stock can tie up cash; no alternative supplier or saving is asserted.

limitations: Historical event; cannot be promoted as current risk.
No supplier identity beyond the named facility is inferred.
No confidential stock, contract, financial or customer facts are assumed.
Management options are analytical considerations, not documented Apple decisions.
No independent opportunity is established by this source.
isolation: Read-only public case. Never inserted into the private twin or decision journal.
